bio: Volcanic park with a crater lake, lava canals and caves, co-managed with Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners.
Crater lake in Budj Bim National Park, walkable from the campground, with a lava canal circuit past Tunnel Cave.
gaps: Lookout viewing platform is closed as structurally unsafe; bio avoids promising it.

bio: Glenelg River gorge cut through limestone, with riverside camping, canoeing and part of the Great South West Walk.
Show cave in Lower Glenelg National Park, 150 m long, with cave coral, rimstone pools and saw-toothed shawls.
gaps: Reported closed until late 2026, reopening unconfirmed, so no guided tour promised; price not found; wiki title is singular 'Princess Margaret Rose Cave'; pin is a round memory pin and needs resolve-pin.

bio: Dormant volcano crater near Warrnambool where emus, kangaroos and koalas live, with walks to the peak.
gaps: Unclear whether the Parks Victoria 'area is closed' banner applies.

bio: Brackish volcanic crater lake near Camperdown, about 66 m deep, paired with neighbouring Lake Gnotuk.
gaps: No sourced visitor activities (walks, swimming, water-skiing); thin facts.

bio: Hypersaline crater lake near Camperdown, about twice as salty as seawater, beside Lake Bullen Merri.
Western District town on the southern shore of Lake Colac, about 150 km south-west of Melbourne.
gaps: Facts give no visitor draw; bio is location only. Draft's claim of being the main Otways town is unsourced.

bio: Box-Ironbark park south of St Arnaud with 275 native plant species, ridge lookouts and a 2.8 km reservoir walk.
gaps: Closure banner on park page unverified.

bio: Guido van Helten's farmers on four 1939 silos, Victoria's first silo artwork and the Silo Art Trail's inspiration.
Geoffrey Carran's art on a 28 m silo with a lookout tower and internal light art reached by lift or stairs.
gaps: Tower and internal viewing fee and hours unverified.

bio: Kaff-eine's mural on 1939 GrainCorp silos, inspired by the local Mallee environment, on the Silo Art Trail.
Silo mural of a girl swinging from a Mallee eucalypt, looking over Lake Tyrrell, on the Silo Art Trail.
Fintan Magee's 2016 portrait of farmer Nick 'Noodle' Hulland on 35 m silos, the town's most notable feature.
Geoffrey Carran's endangered birds painted on silos among gums, about an hour from Horsham.
Rone's 2017 monochrome portrait of farmers Geoff and Merrilyn Horman on two 1939 silos.
Sam Bates's photo-realistic farmer in a flannelette shirt with his kelpie, painted on the Nullawil silo.
Jack Fran's silo mural of the surveyors in the South Australia-Victoria border dispute, beside a grand railway station.
Eight small field-bin murals around town celebrate the Mallee's endangered species, with a carpark and picnic area.
gaps: Not a single large silo mural; consider renaming (e.g. Woomelang Mini Silo Art Trail).

bio: Stop on the Silo Art Trail, a series of large murals on grain silos linking Wimmera Mallee towns.
gaps: Only trail-level fact sourced; no source for the Sheep Hills mural itself (artist, subject).

bio: Silo and town murals in St Arnaud, near the Wimmera Mallee's Silo Art Trail of large-scale grain silo murals.
gaps: No source found for St Arnaud's silo or town murals; only trail-level fact. Placement unsupported until sourced.

bio: Museum of wool, fibre and textiles in the former Dennys, Lascelles woolstore, opened in 1988.
Granite peaks rising from the plains, with Flinders Peak views to Melbourne and Geelong and over 50 km of trails.
gaps: Unconfirmed whether any area is currently closed.

bio: Botanic garden in Eastern Park, established in 1850 and the fourth oldest in Australia.
